_comment: Reviewed replacement for the uploaded kit's config/permissions.example.json. NOT active: activating a policy that governs the agent is an Owner action, so this is committed for review and adopted by copying to .claude/settings.json deliberately. Deny wins over allow in every mode.
_why_this_differs_from_the_kit: The kit allowed Read(**) and defended it in a note: 'Restricting reads makes the agent guess, which is worse.' That trades a real boundary for a convenience. Read(**) grants the host filesystem - every repository, every home directory, every mounted volume - and the deny list beside it is an enumeration of the secrets someone happened to think of. A new credential path, a new provider's config file, a colleague's checkout: all readable, none denied.
Reads are scoped to roots instead. The agent still reads dependency source, which was the stated need, because the dependency roots are named explicitly.

This file is defence in depth and nothing more. It is a policy a process consults, so it is only as good as that process. The boundary is the container: mounts, namespaces, UID/GID, seccomp, AppArmor/SELinux and network policy. A permission JSON is not a security boundary and must never be the only thing standing between an agent and a credential.

permissions._read_note: Three roots, each with a reason. `./**` is the assigned task worktree, which is the only repository the sandbox is given - not the host tree. The other two are the dependency source the kit's note was actually asking for: reading how an installed library behaves is legitimate and does not require the home directory. `/proc/*/environ` is denied explicitly because a process's own environment is a credential store that no path glob would otherwise cover.
permissions._enforcement_note: Every deny above must ALSO hold when this file is absent. `Bash(docker:*)` is denied here and the socket is simply not mounted; `Read(~/.ssh/**)` is denied here and the home directory is simply not bind-mounted. If a control appears only in this file, it is not yet enforced.
